name: moods
character: What each mood in the intent vocabulary asks a piece's inferred chemistry to do. The target is built from the mood's own valence/arousal coordinates (references/data/presets/intent/valence_arousal.json) by two axis shifts, with a per-mood override only where a two-axis model plainly fails - so any mood the intent vocabulary can resolve has a target without a hand-written table.
provenance: Starting values [start]: the axis shifts and every override are modelling choices, not measurements. They say what a piece of that mood should contain, and docs/NEUROCHEMICAL-AFFECT-PLAN.md section 5 explains why the layer is ingredient-level only (individual differences dominate: 5-10 % of listeners are music-anhedonic).

arousal.why: [start] high arousal in this repo's coordinates means more density, level and onset rate (affect.arc_arousal), which is the same material that drives the motor and arrival pools.

valence.why: [start] the valence axis here is mode minus clash, so a positive valence is expected to read as warmer, more consonant and better resolved.

grief.why: a two-axis model puts grief near zero affiliation; the sad-music literature and the mode/valence proxy both point the other way, toward a warm, voice-like, static piece.

sad.why: as grief: sad pieces are slower and less motor-driven than the arousal axis alone predicts.

melancholy.why: as grief: the axis model under-reads the affiliative pull of a slow minor piece.

scary.why: horror wants no comfort and no come-down: the piece should end unresolved, which the recovery axis of a negative-valence state does not express.

dark_epic.why: as scary: threat without warmth, and the ending is the peak, not a release.

tense.why: suspense is carried to the last bar by design; a resolved ending is a different brief.

calm.why: calm is defined by the absence of drive and load, which a straight read of low arousal still leaves too high.

dreamy.why: dreamlike states are static and warm; the arousal axis alone would ask for a pulse the brief does not want.

epic.why: an epic is a long build with several states; the axis model has no room to ask for length.

triumphant.why: a triumph is prepared by a long build; the arousal axis alone has no room to ask for length.

majestic.why: as triumphant: grandeur is a build, not a level.

focused.why: concentration wants little tension and few states; a two-axis point cannot say 'stay in one place'.

excess_why: [start] the row asks whether the piece has what the mood needs: falling short counts fully, exceeding the target counts half, so a piece with more build than the mood asks for is not scored as wrong as one with none.
why: [start] at most three emotion words are averaged into one target; more than three are different briefs and their average is nobody's piece.
